SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349


PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
INTERVENOR AARON EDWARD HOWTON'S RESPONSE TO APPLICANTS' OBJECTIONS TO, AND MOTION TO STRIKE, INTERVENOR TESTIMONY
TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:
Intervenor Nelda Howton files this Response to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation's Objections to, and Motion to Strike, Intervenor Testimony. Mrs. Howton respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges deny the motion to strike his Direct Testimony, or alternatively reserve ruling until the hearing so that she may sponsor her testimony under oath, be subject to voir dire if requested, and submit to cross-examination.
I. SUMMARY OF RESPONSE
Applicants appear to seek to strike or limit portions of intervenor testimony on hearsay and qualification grounds. As applied to Mr. Howton, that objection should be denied. Mrs. Howton's Direct Testimony is not an out-of-court statement being offered through some other witness; it is her own prefiled direct testimony in this contested case. She is prepared to appear in person, swear that the testimony is true and accurate, and be cross-examined. Under SOAH and PUC procedure, written direct testimony may be admitted into evidence after the witness is sworn and identifies the testimony as the testimony she would give orally.
Mrs. Howton’s education, training, and experience directly related to this matter is addressed in her testimony, including operations on her farm, the proposed close proximity of the 765kV transmission line to her home, her concern for her animals and her community . Applicants may challenge the weight to be given to that testimony through cross-examination, but the testimony should not be stricken in advance.
II. ARGUMENT
A. Prefiled Direct Testimony Is Proper Evidence When Sponsored by the Witness.
SOAH Rule 155.429 expressly allows direct testimony to be filed in writing before the hearing in narrative or question-and-answer form. Once the witness is sworn and identifies the written testimony as a true record of what the witness would have testified to orally, the written testimony may be admitted into evidence as if read or presented orally. See 1 Tex. Admin. Code § 155.429(c)(1)(A)-(D).
The PUC's rule governing written testimony is consistent with that procedure. Written testimony may be received as an exhibit and incorporated into the record without being read aloud, provided the witness is sworn, confirms that the testimony is true and accurate, and submits to cross-examination, clarifying questions, redirect examination, and recross-examination. See 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 22.225(b).
For that reason, Mrs. Howton's filed Direct Testimony should not be characterized as inadmissible hearsay merely because it was filed before the hearing. It is the method ordered and permitted for presenting direct testimony in this case. Mrs. Howton will sponsor the testimony under oath and will be available for cross-examination.
B. Mrs. Howton Is Qualified by Knowledge, Skill, Experience, Training, and Education.
Texas Rule of Evidence 702 permits testimony from a witness qualified by knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education if the testimony will assist the trier of fact in understanding the evidence or determining a fact issue. Mrs. Howton is not offering unsupported rumor. She is offering opinions and observations based on approximately thirty years of living and observing both her farm and the community.
Mrs. Howton graduated from Texas A&M International University in 1977 with a Bachelor of Science degree in Education and Baylor University in 1989 with a Master of Science degree in Education. 
From 1977 to current 2026, Mrs. Howton has worked in education for the State of Texas, that is 49 years!  She has served as a science instructor, both elementary and high school Principal, Director of Biotechnology for Temple College, and currently Consultant with Educate Texas.
C. The Testimony Is Based on Personal Knowledge and Specialized Experience, Not Mere Hearsay.
To the extent Mrs. Howton testifies about her own property, agricultural operations,  observations, education, employment history, and experience with state laws, that testimony is based on personal knowledge. Such testimony is not hearsay.
To the extent Mrs. Howton relies on technical, scientific, regulatory, or agency materials, such materials may be considered as part of the basis for her opinions and may also be addressed through exhibits, official notice, cross-examination, or argument concerning weight. A blanket hearsay objection should not be used to strike an intervenor's entire testimony where the witness is available to sponsor the testimony and explain the basis for her opinions.
D. Striking the Testimony Would Be Unfairly Prejudicial and Inconsistent With the Development of a Complete Record.
This proceeding concerns a 765-kV transmission line that may materially affect private property, agricultural operations, wildlife habitat, and landowners' use and enjoyment of their land. Mrs. Howton is an affected landowner and intervenor. Her testimony provides relevant facts, observations, and specialized opinions for the Administrative Law Judges and the Commission to consider in evaluating routing issues.
If Applicants believe any particular sentence exceeds the proper scope of Mrs. Howton's expertise, the appropriate remedy is not to strike the testimony in its entirety. The Administrative Law Judges may receive the testimony subject to cross-examination, limit or assign weight to particular opinions, or permit voir dire where appropriate. Mrs. Howton expressly agrees to appear, be sworn, authenticate his testimony, and answer cross-examination.
III. PRAYER
For the reasons stated above, Intervenor Nelda Howton respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges deny Applicants' motion to strike her Direct Testimony and overrule the hearsay objection as applied to her testimony. In the alternative, Mrs. Howton requests that the Administrative Law Judges reserve ruling until the hearing, allow voir dire if requested, allow her to sponsor her testimony under oath, and admit her testimony subject to cross-examination and the Administrative Law Judges' determination of the appropriate weight to be given to the testimony.
Mrs. Howton further requests all other relief, at law or in equity, to which she may be justly entitled.
Respectfully submitted,
